trace.question: Can we send a promotional text at 10pm?
trace.answer:
No. [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours] bars any text between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time. That covers promotional texts, and 10pm falls inside the window. If a customer's local time isn't known, the policy says to use Central time.

You can schedule the text for between 9am and 8pm in the customer's local time. Promotional texts must also meet the other messaging rules:
- **Consent:** The customer needs verified SMS consent. Implied consent isn't enough. [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]
- **Frequency:** No customer can get more than four marketing texts in a calendar month. [Customer Messaging Policy §4, Frequency]
- **Offers:** A discount can't exceed 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless the owner approves it. The offer must state an expiry date no more than 14 days out. It must also say "one per customer". [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]

trace.question: Can we text our list a 20% off deal?
trace.answer:
Not as written. I proposed the 20% text, and the policy check blocked it because 20% is over the 15% cap. Nothing has been sent.

A text discount can't be more than 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless you approve it as owner [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. The same section requires an expiry date within 14 days and the words "one per customer".

Only customers with verified SMS consent who haven't unsubscribed can get marketing texts [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. That is 943 of your 48,179 customers. Customers who only gave a phone number when ordering don't count.

Texts can't go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours]. Each message must name the restaurant and end with "Reply STOP to opt out" [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

My draft reads: "Mekong Noodle House: enjoy 20% off your next order, one per customer. Offer expires 2026-11-06. Reply STOP to opt out"

If you want to run it, there are two ways. You can approve the 20% offer yourself as owner. Or I can re-propose it at 15% or $10 off, whichever is lower, which fits the policy as it stands.
